description.purpose: Resolve an authorized scanner non-delivery dispute and increase the existing Silver Rewards Card limit, preserving eligibility through outcome-sensitive sequencing.

user_scenario.instructions:
You are Leila Haddad, a 54-year-old small-business bookkeeper in Madison, Wisconsin. Your November statement prompted this call. Begin: “I need to dispute an undelivered scanner charge on my Silver Rewards Card. I also want a higher limit so I can buy a replacement while this is sorted out. Can you help with both?”

Answer relevant questions without volunteering all details. For identity or registered contacts, provide the requested information: Leila Haddad; birth date 07/22/1971; 608-555-0146; leila.haddad@example.net; 1846 Maple Grove Lane, Madison, WI 53704.

When asked about the purchase, explain that you authorized Cedar Scan Supply's $2,864.75 charge on 10/08/2025 for an archival document scanner. Delivery was expected within two weeks. You noticed the problem on 10/29/2025 and emailed on 10/29, 11/04, and 11/12 without replies. Neither goods nor a refund arrived. You want a full-refund non-delivery dispute, not a fraud allegation or a guaranteed final refund. When asked about the limit, say your current limit is $12,000 and you want a new total of $18,000 on this existing card for the replacement purchase. You have had it about a year and paid on time. Keep the card active; do not cancel or replace it.

If asked for card digits, say the card is not with you and request secure lookup help. Use the lookup when offered and report only the digits it returns. Do not guess identifiers, policy thresholds, eligibility, or processing order. Once the agent establishes your identity, identifies the correct card and scanner charge, and explains a service consistent with your requests, authorize that service.

For any conflicting proposal—including a different product, smaller refund request, fraud claim, replacement, cancellation, or abandoning either request—decline permission and identify the affected goal. If it already happened, ask for correction or review of the unresolved outcome, without guessing a policy remedy. You cannot tell whether filing first is wrong; do not challenge that order alone. If told it prevents the increase, apply the same rule rather than agreeing to abandon it. If filing is complete but the increase is refused, say the limit request remains unresolved and ask for review; do not suggest erasing the dispute.

Accept completion only when the agent confirms the requested new total limit is effective, the full-refund non-delivery dispute is filed for the scanner, the card remains usable, and the temporary-credit outcome is explained without presenting the investigation as a final refund. A submission or promise to finish later is insufficient. Then briefly thank the agent and end with:
###STOP###
